name: Carta Nueva
classification_notes: Spencerian-style pointed-nib script digitised from an 1851 Barcelona calligraphy booklet. Firm downstrokes, tapering hairline upstrokes drawn at 4096 UPM, and ornate uppercase loops distinguish it from simpler cursive faces. Offered in five optical sizes rather than weight variants; not a connecting script in the conventional sense — each optical size is a distinct master tuned for its intended size range. Multi-directional typesetting support (vertical setting) was a stated design goal.
summary: A digital re-imagination of a pointed-nib calligraphic model from 1851 Barcelona, offered across five optical sizes from intimate text to grand display.
description: Carta Nueva was drawn by Sharp Type senior designer My-Lan Thuong from an antique calligraphy booklet found at a Madrid fair, tracing an 1851 Barcelona hand whose original author is unknown. The design preserves Spencerian rhythm through controlled downstrokes and hairline upstrokes built at 4096 UPM, with uppercase letters carrying ornate loops and arabesques. Five optical sizes give it range from correspondence-scale text to headline work, and an extended Latin glyph set of 1,698 characters covers Vietnamese, Polish, Icelandic and beyond.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describes Carta Nueva as "poised and lively" – a script that is "smart without being elitist and elegant without pretension." The foundry frames it as a typeface for design at all scales, built to feel genuinely handwritten rather than mechanically cursive, with broad Latin coverage added to every Sharp Type release since its 2020 launch.

name: Ceraph
classification_notes: Sharp Type describe Ceraph as a "contemporary display semi-serif". The flared stroke endings produce an engraved quality distinct from traditional bracketed serifs. Uppercase proportions reference classical Roman inscriptional capitals; lowercase draws from calligraphic practice. Influenced by Hermann Zapf, Giovan Francesco Cresci, Jakob Erbar and Canela. The name fuses "seraph" and "serif".
summary: A display flared serif by Emma Piercy that pairs Roman inscriptional capitals with calligraphic lowercase forms, released through Sharp Type in 2024.
description: Ceraph began as a sketch in 2018 and was officially released through Sharp Type in November 2024. Its flared stroke endings give the letterforms an engraved, chiselled quality, while the uppercase draws on classical Roman proportions and the lowercase follows a calligraphic logic. At two styles – Regular and Italic – it is lean on weights but precise in character, aimed at display and titling work that wants both presence and refinement.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type position Ceraph as a contemporary display semi-serif with monumental presence and main-character energy. The finely chiselled forms suit any setting that calls for subtlety and elegance.

name: Cordier Script
classification_notes: Historical revival rooted in 17th-century French italic-bastarde calligraphy. Diagonal-axis letterforms with inverted thick-and-thin modulation, serpentine upward sweeps, and multiple half-letter forms enabling connections at varying heights. Extensive contextual alternates via OpenType. Two distinct style cuts: unconnected (Regular) and fully connected (Linked).
summary: A calligraphic connecting script by Benjamin Gomez reviving the 17th-century italic-bastarde penmanship of Louis Barbedor, with serpentine letterforms, inverted stroke contrast and rich contextual variation across two styles.
description: Cordier Script takes its name from the engraver who produced the plates for Louis Barbedor's 1650 French calligraphy manual, and it translates that chancery penmanship into a contemporary typeface with natural momentum. Benjamin Gomez drew each letter with numerous contextual alternates and multiple half-letter forms, allowing connections at varying heights so text flows with the suppleness of actual handwriting. It comes in two styles, Regular and Linked, and suits display headlines, editorial layouts and branding equally well.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describe Cordier Script as channelling the virtuosic calligraphy of Louis Barbedor, the 17th-century French master penman, reimagined as a contemporary script. The family draws from the intricate engraved plates of Barbedor's "Les écritures financière et italienne-bastarde" (1650), combining historical elegance with a lithe modern rhythm through comprehensive OpenType features and broad global language support.

name: DOSS Collection
classification_notes: Unicase display superfamily of four stylistically distinct faces; exaggerated geometric construction with unexpectedly round counterforms; no traditional weight axis — instead nine named stylistic variants across Exaflop (three widths), Acid, Plexus and Problem (four variants including outlined and rounded). Traced to an obscure Hollenstein phototypesetting face by Emeric Dorr, reworked to invert '70s and '80s futurist clichés.
summary: A techno-futurist display collection of four typefaces by Marc Rouault, unified by exaggerated geometry and unicase letterforms, with a lineage traced to an obscure Hollenstein phototypesetting face.
description: Released in 2024 after five years in development, DOSS comprises Exaflop (in three widths), Acid, Plexus and Problem (four stylistic variants including an outlined and a rounded version). Each face is built around exaggerated geometric structures and unexpectedly round counterforms, drawing from construction and hi-fi audio brand logotypes as well as '90s rave aesthetics and '80s sci-fi. It works best in headline and identity contexts where an explicit genre allegiance is the point.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describes DOSS as a techno-futurist collection inspired by construction and hi-fi audio brand logotypes, referencing '90s rave culture and '80s sci-fi tropes. The four faces share exaggerated geometric structures, unexpectedly round counterforms and unicase character sets. Marc Rouault's starting point was an obscure phototypesetting face from the Hollenstein collection by Emeric Dorr; he retrofitted and extended that design logic while inverting the visual clichés of futurist typography from the '70s and '80s.

name: Alpes
classification_notes: A single-width condensed grotesque characterised by switchbacking curves, sharp angles and steely straight lines. Sits at the intersection of editorial display and technical use, with enough formal tension to avoid the blandness common in utilitarian condensed grotesques.
summary: A condensed grotesque superfamily co-designed by Image Format's Johan Mossé and Quentin Berthelot, balancing compact form against expressive personality across six weights with roman and italic cuts and a matching mono companion.
description: Alpes is a condensed grotesque built on switchbacking curves, sharp angles and steely straight lines. The result is a typeface with a compact footprint that carries genuine personality, equally at home in editorial display settings and technical contexts. It is the second collaboration between Sharp Type and Paris studio Image Format, and comes paired with Alpes Mono for fixed-width use.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describes Alpes as a pristine, all-terrain typeface extending the tradition of condensed grotesque forebears while opting for distinction without sacrificing readability. A balance of extremes: compact build with expressive personality, working at scales from monumental to miniature across editorial and technical contexts.

name: Eterne Text
classification_notes: Low-contrast text serif with shallow-shouldered arches and evenly proportioned terminals. References W.A. Dwiggins' Marionette Formula and Miller & Richard's Old Style Antique No. 7. Designed as the text-optimised counterpart to Eterne Display, prioritising scalability and sustained readability over display drama.
summary: A low-contrast old-style text serif by Kia Tasbihgou, its lively letterforms informed by Dwiggins' Marionette Formula and the old-style tradition of Miller & Richard.
description: Eterne Text is the body-copy counterpart to Eterne Display, a two-family pairing where the character of the broader Eterne family is translated into a system suited to longer reading. Shallow-shouldered arches, low contrast and evenly proportioned terminals recall Miller & Richard's Old Style Antique No. 7, while unexpected cuts and curves rooted in Dwiggins' Marionette Formula give the letterforms a lively tension between space and counter-space. Four weights with matching italics make up the eight-style family.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describes Eterne Text as bringing refined clarity of construction to an unconventional model, translating the drama and gesture of the Eterne family into a system that is eminently scalable. The letterforms take cues from the Marionette Formula proposed by W.A. Dwiggins, with unexpected cuts and curves that draw attention to the push-and-pull of space and counter-space. Engineered by Calvin Kwok with kerning by Igino Marini.

name: Ghost Display Mono
classification_notes: Monospace display variant within the Ghost Superfamily, a humanist sans-serif with fixed-width spacing optimised for large-size and coding contexts. Part of a variable font designspace with optical size and mono axes. The broader superfamily spans proportional (Display, Text) and fixed-width (SemiMono, Mono) subfamilies, all sharing the same underlying humanist sans skeleton drawn in the tradition of Johnston and Optima.
summary: Ghost Display Mono is Sharp Type's fixed-width display cut of their humanist sans superfamily, designed for large-scale typesetting and coding contexts where character equality is needed without sacrificing warmth.
description: Ghost Display Mono is the monospaced, display-scale member of Sharp Type's Ghost Superfamily – a 72-style humanist sans built over four years and released in 2022. Rooted in the tradition of Johnston and Optima, Ghost carries warmth and historical depth while remaining functionally neutral; the Mono cut locks all glyphs to equal width, making it well suited to data, code, and editorial settings where rhythm and alignment matter. The superfamily spans a variable designspace with optical size and mono axes, allowing the Display Mono to sit within a coherent system stretching from headline proportional to small-text fixed-width.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describes Ghost as a back-to-the-roots take on the humanist sans genre, drawing on Roman inscriptional lettering, Edward Johnston's 1916 typeface and Hermann Zapf's Optima to codify the category for contemporary use. The superfamily – developed with My-Lan Thuong, Léna Le Pommelet and Daniel Veneklaas – integrates 72 static styles and a single variable font spanning display, text and coding functions via seamless optical-size and mono axes.

name: Ghost Display
classification_notes: Low-to-medium contrast humanist sans-serif with open apertures and warm terminals. References Roman inscriptional lettering, Edward Johnston's 1916 typeface and Hermann Zapf's Optima. Variable font with an optical size axis spanning display to text and a mono axis producing SemiMono and full Mono variants. Display optical cut of the 72-style Ghost superfamily; originally released 2022 as Ghost, revised and extended in 2026 as Ghost Display with a sixth weight added.
designer: Lucas Sharp, My-Lan Thuong, Léna Le Pommelet, Daniel Veneklaas
summary: A studied humanist sans rooted in Johnston, Optima and Roman inscriptional lettering, released as a 72-style variable superfamily with display, text and mono optical cuts.
description: Ghost Display is the headline optical cut of Sharp Type's Ghost superfamily, a humanist sans drawing references from Roman inscriptional letters, Edward Johnston's 1916 typeface and Hermann Zapf's Optima. Available in six weights with roman and italic styles, it belongs to a 72-style family spanning Display, Text and Mono subfamilies, all connected through a variable designspace with continuous optical size and mono axes. Developed over four years by a four-person team, it is designed for equal composure at editorial scale, brand identity and screen use.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describe Ghost as a back-to-the-roots take on the humanist sans genre and a meditation on the ephemeral nature of normalcy, arguing that its DNA of neutrality lets it function in any context, from web and print to signage.

name: Alpes Mono
classification_notes: Monospaced companion to the Alpes condensed grotesque superfamily. Draws from the contrasted grotesque lineage but departs toward a more expressive, angular character. Switchbacking curves and steely straight lines distinguish it within the condensed mono genre. Designed for use from editorial display down to technical applications.
designer: Johan Mossé & Quentin Berthelot (Image Format); kerning by Igino Marini
summary: The monospaced companion to Alpes, bringing sharp angles, switchbacking curves and condensed grotesque personality to fixed-width type for editorial and technical use.
description: Alpes Mono is the monospaced companion to the Alpes condensed grotesque superfamily, a joint venture between Sharp Type and Paris-based studio Image Format. Designed by Johan Mossé and Quentin Berthelot, it draws from the contrasted grotesque tradition but pushes further: compact proportions, sharp angles and steely straight lines give it a character that works from large editorial headlines down to code-adjacent contexts. Six weights with matching italics, totalling 12 styles, make it a flexible choice for any typographic system requiring fixed-width type with genuine distinction.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describe Alpes as arising from the bedrock principles of contrasted grotesques but arriving somewhere more adventurous – a pristine, all-terrain typeface sculpted by and for designers, extending its genre forebears without sacrificing readability. With switchbacking curves, sharp angles and steely straight lines, it balances compact build against expressive personality, working at scales from monumental to miniature across editorial and technical contexts. Alpes Mono adds fixed-width spacing to that formula.

name: Eterne Display
classification_notes: A compact, condensed serif display typeface inspired by printed magician's ephemera and French titling types – specifically Deberny & Peignot's Elzévir Gras Allongé. Designer Kia Tasbihgou introduces idiosyncratic incisions and gestural letterform twists that distinguish it from conventional display revivals. The family comes in 6 styles (specific weight names unconfirmed at time of research). It is inherently compact and narrow by design rather than offering a separate condensed sub-family, and pairs with the companion Eterne Text (8 styles) for reading-size applications.
summary: A compact condensed serif built for titling, drawing on French display type tradition and magician's ephemera, with idiosyncratic cuts and gestural letterform twists.
description: Eterne Display takes its cues from printed magician's ephemera and the condensed French titling types of Deberny & Peignot's Elzévir Gras Allongé. Designer Kia Tasbihgou works idiosyncratic incisions and gestural twists into the letterforms, giving the family its own character without sacrificing legibility at display scale. It sits alongside the companion Eterne Text, which applies the same sensibility at reading sizes with refined clarity.
foundry_blurb: A compact and springy suite of titling fonts that began as a direct response to printed magician's ephemera, taking cues from French titling types like Deberny & Peignot's Elzévir Gras Allongé. Its condensed forms are gracefully articulated with idiosyncratic incisions and gestural twists on convention, suited to editorial contexts where prestige, pragmatism, and space are at a premium. Slyly intricate and fiercely structured, Eterne holds an elegant tension balancing bold form with functional clarity.

name: Ghost Text
classification_notes: Humanist sans-serif tuned for text and UI settings. Draws on Roman inscriptional lettering and early 20th-century grotesks (particularly Franklin Gothic's subtle stroke modulation). Part of the Ghost Superfamily alongside Ghost Display; shares the same underlying DNA but with optical adjustments for small-scale legibility and screen use. Spans a mono axis across three subfamilies: proportional (Ghost Text), semi-monospaced (Ghost Text SemiMono), and monospaced (Ghost Text Mono). Available as a variable font integrating optical size and mono axes in a single designspace.
summary: The text branch of Sharp Type's Ghost Superfamily, designed by My-Lan Thuong for UI and screen use across proportional, semi-mono and mono subfamilies.
description: Ghost Text is the small-scale counterpart to Ghost Display, retaining the humanist warmth and idiosyncrasy of the broader Ghost Superfamily while optimising optical settings for legibility at text sizes. Designed by My-Lan Thuong, it spans three subfamilies along a mono axis – proportional, semi-monospaced, and monospaced – making it an unusually unified system for products that need editorial and code environments to share a typeface. All three subfamilies are available as a variable font, with five weights and italics, integrated into a single designspace alongside Ghost Display.
foundry_blurb: Ghost Text brings the genetic idiosyncrasies of the Ghost Display family to text and coding contexts. As a utilitarian humanist sans built for on-screen optimisation, it retains the warmth and striking personality of the display sibling while maximising readability at small sizes. Its seamless variable axes scale across text and coding functions, with the mono axis unifying proportional, semi-mono and monospaced setting in one coherent system.

name: Ghost Text SemiMono
classification_notes: Humanist sans-serif with a semi-monospaced glyph rhythm. Sits between the proportional Ghost Text and the fully fixed-width Ghost Text Mono. The Ghost superfamily traces its roots to Roman inscriptional lettering, Johnston's 1916 Underground type, and Optima (1958). The SemiMono variant is calibrated for screen reading where a uniform character cadence aids scanning without the rigidity of full monospace.
summary: The semi-monospaced text branch of Sharp Type's Ghost superfamily, occupying the middle ground between proportional editorial type and fixed-width code fonts.
description: Ghost Text SemiMono is one of six members in Sharp Type's Ghost Superfamily, which spans display, text and coding functions across a single variable designspace. Its character rhythm is more uniform than a proportional sans but stops short of true monospace, making it suited to interfaces and publications where running text and technical content share the page. The design roots back to Roman inscriptional writing and mid-century humanist classics, given a sharp contemporary edge by Lucas Sharp and his team.
foundry_blurb: Part of the Ghost Superfamily developed over four years by Lucas Sharp, My-Lan Thuong, Léna Le Pommelet and Daniel Veneklaas. Ghost Text SemiMono is one of six subfamilies in a 72-style variable superfamily that scales from headline display to screen text to code-ready mono within a single designspace. The family was originally released in 2022 as Ghost Display and expanded to its current breadth in 2026.
designer: Lucas Sharp, My-Lan Thuong, Léna Le Pommelet, Daniel Veneklaas

name: Greenstone
classification_notes: Stone carving-inspired display serif with low-contrast horizontal strokes and high-contrast delicate serifs, drawing from flat-brush calligraphy and lapidary inscriptional lettering. Both cuts carry subtle forward slants – Regular at 2°, Italic at 5° – rather than a conventional upright roman and separate sloped variant. Large flaring capitals and expansive serifs give it a distinctive inscriptional weight.
summary: A lapidary display serif by Connor Davenport, drawing on Oscar Ogg's mid-century vernacular lettering and New England stone-carving tradition.
description: Greenstone bridges inscriptional precision with the fluid ductus of flat-brush calligraphy, producing a serif of unusual historic character. The Regular carries a near-imperceptible 2° slant and the Italic leans only 5°, with the more fluid construction of broad-nib penmanship. Large, flaring capitals and delicate expansive serifs give it a quality that reads as historically literate without feeling archaic.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describes Greenstone as interpreting Oscar Ogg's vernacular lettering through American and British stone-carving tradition – particularly the work of John Howard Benson and David Kindersley. Connor Davenport visited the John Stevens Shop in Newport, the oldest continuously operating stone-carving studio in the United States, studying details such as connected Gs and unusual serifs on historic gravestones as the basis for the design.

name: Ghost Display SemiMono
classification_notes: Humanist sans-serif at display optical size with semi-monospaced spacing. Sits on the mono axis between the proportional Ghost Display and the fully monospaced Ghost Display Mono within a single variable designspace. Draws on Roman inscriptional lettering, Edward Johnston's 1916 typeface, and Hermann Zapf's Optima as historical references.
summary: The semi-monospaced display cut of Sharp Type's Ghost superfamily, sitting between fully proportional and fully monospaced on the family's variable mono axis.
description: Ghost Display SemiMono is one of six subfamilies in the Ghost superfamily, which spans 72 styles across display and text optical sizes and three points on a mono axis. Its spacing is more uniform than the proportional Ghost Display but less rigid than Ghost Display Mono, making it useful wherever a degree of rhythmic consistency is wanted at large scale without sacrificing the warmth of humanist construction. Developed by Lucas Sharp with My-Lan Thuong, Léna Le Pommelet, and Daniel Veneklaas, the SemiMono subfamilies were introduced as part of the V.2 expansion in 2026.
foundry_blurb: Ghost is Sharp Type's back-to-the-roots take on the humanist sans genre: a meditation on neutrality and normalcy that draws from Johnston and Optima while asserting its own warm, adaptable identity. The Display SemiMono occupies the midpoint of the family's mono axis, part of a complete variable designspace that scales from editorial display to body text to monospaced code.
designer: Lucas Sharp, My-Lan Thuong, Léna Le Pommelet, Daniel Veneklaas

name: Hauss
classification_notes: Early 19th-century Monotype grotesque revival. Thin weight sparked by a specimen at The Letterform Archive in 2022; heavier weights (Bold, Black) reference Akzidenz Grotesk and Genzch & Heyse Blockschrift. Italics use a steep 12-degree angle with rotated logic rather than a pure oblique slant. 14 styles across 7 weights, roman and italic.
summary: A workhorse grotesque drawn from 19th-century Monotype sources, refined across seven weights with characterful italics pitched at a steep 12-degree angle.
description: Hauss is a sans-serif grotesque designed by Justin Sloane and Huw Williams, developed over several years as a personal design tool before being released through Sharp Type in October 2024. Its Thin weight draws on an early Monotype grotesque specimen discovered at The Letterform Archive in 2022, while the heavier weights shift register, referencing Akzidenz Grotesk and Genzch & Heyse Blockschrift for a more display-oriented character. The italics are set at a steep 12-degree angle using rotated rather than oblique logic, preserving the roundness of the roman across the range.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describes Hauss and its companion face Raum as "a sturdy design tool and an exercise in psychedelic retrofuturism" — two typefaces that span the distance from purely utilitarian to bombastically experimental, conceived as an all-in-one visual system.

name: Ghost Text Mono
classification_notes: Monospaced humanist sans-serif, the coding-oriented member of Sharp Type's Ghost superfamily. Design roots trace to Roman inscriptional lettering and Edward Johnston's 1916 typeface. Fixed-width proportions for code editors and technical environments, paired with a SemiMono sub-family that sits between proportional and full monospace. Released in May 2026 as part of a major Ghost superfamily expansion (72 styles across 6 sub-families), all integrated into a single variable designspace with optical size and mono axes. 12 static styles per sub-family (6 weights × upright + italic).
designer: Lucas Sharp, My-Lan Thuong, Léna Le Pommelet, Daniel Veneklaas
summary: The coding companion within the Ghost superfamily, carrying humanist warmth into fixed-width environments across five weights with italic and a SemiMono variant.
description: Ghost Text Mono is the monospaced sub-family of Sharp Type's Ghost superfamily, a four-year collaborative project by Lucas Sharp, My-Lan Thuong, Léna Le Pommelet and Daniel Veneklaas. Released in May 2026 alongside Ghost Display and Ghost Text, it provides five weights with italic counterparts, plus a SemiMono variant that bridges full fixed-width and proportional spacing. The design inherits Ghost's humanist character, grounded in Roman inscriptional lettering and Edward Johnston's 1916 typeface, giving it more warmth than a mechanically constructed coding font.
foundry_blurb: Ghost Text Mono covers the Text Mono and Text SemiMono sub-families of the Ghost series. Through seamless variable axes scaling across display, text and coding functions, the Ghost Superfamily spans seventy-two styles integrated into a single variable designspace — a comprehensive design toolkit built from a back-to-the-roots study of the humanist sans genre.

name: Record Laser
classification_notes: Angular display sans-serif with dynamic width variations and extreme geometric construction, drawing direct influence from Roger Excoffon's Antique Olive Nord and Dick Jensen's Serpentine. Designed specifically for display and branding contexts requiring a charged 1980s retro-futuristic aesthetic. One half of the Record Superfamily; sibling family Record Disc takes a softer, more versatile approach.
summary: A sharp, angular display sans by Image Format for Sharp Type, pushing width dynamics and geometric extremes to channel the retro-futuristic graphic energy of the 1980s.
description: Released in February 2025, Record Laser is one half of Sharp Type's Record Superfamily, the other being the softer and more versatile Record Disc. Its letterforms are defined by exaggerated width variation and extreme angularity, drawing direct influence from Roger Excoffon's Antique Olive Nord and Dick Jensen's Serpentine. The family runs to five weights with matching italics, making it a focused tool for branding and display work that calls for a period-specific, high-voltage edge.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describe Record Laser as having a sharp, unapologetically retro-futuristic aesthetic, with dynamic width and angularity that push design logic to the extreme. The foundry positions it as capturing the bold spirit of 1980s futurism, citing Antique Olive Nord and Serpentine as the historical foundations of the Record family.

name: Octave
classification_notes: A modern neo-grotesque that draws on mid-twentieth century Swiss grotesques (Univers, Haas Unica lineage) while reexamining their structural conventions. Clean construction, regularised letterforms, and a considered balance between historical grotesque sensibility and contemporary refinement. No overt quirks or revival nostalgia.
summary: A considered neo-grotesque from Josh Finklea that revisits mid-century sans-serif principles without nostalgia, offering 12 styles for branding and editorial use.
description: Octave is a 2022 neo-grotesque from Josh Finklea, released through Sharp Type. It takes the structural logic of mid-twentieth century sans-serifs as a starting point, then reexamines letterform decisions with fresh eyes rather than reverting to historical precedent. The result is a clean, harmonious grotesque that sits comfortably between Swiss rigour and contemporary workability.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describes Octave as a reconsideration of the modern sans serif: one that respects the reliability of 1900s grotesque tradition while allowing structure and aesthetics to be logically refined. Josh Finklea's love of classical music shaped the art direction, and the face was engineered by Connor Davenport with kerning by Igino Marini.

name: Raum
classification_notes: A sans-serif display typeface built around an extreme inktrap motif, designed to push the contemporaneous display inktrap convention toward psychedelic retrofuturist territory. References include the Arnold Böcklin typeface, Leo Maggs's Westminster, Stan Davis's Amelia, and Paul Nicholson's 1991 Aphex Twin logo. Redrawn to mirror the weight range and proportions of its companion, Hauss. Includes Böcklin alternates as a stylistic set. 7 styles total; italic cuts feature a steep 12-degree angle with a rotated rather than pure oblique construction.
summary: An extreme inktrap display face that pairs with the Hauss workhorse sans, drawing on Aphex Twin-era retrofuturism and Art Nouveau to push the inktrap motif well beyond utility.
description: Raum is the display counterpart to Hauss, sharing its weight range and proportions while taking the inktrap concept in a distinctly psychedelic direction. Conceived by Justin Sloane in 2018 as an unrealised custom project and redrawn with Huw Williams to align with Hauss, it draws from Paul Nicholson's 1991 Aphex Twin logo, the Arnold Böcklin typeface, and Leo Maggs's Westminster. The family ships with Böcklin alternates that lean into the Art Nouveau flavour, and italic cuts use a steep 12-degree angle with a rotated rather than oblique construction.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describe Raum as representing a kind of destruction, pushing the contemporaneous display inktrap motif into uncharted territory by defining polarities from utilitarian to bombastically unconventional. The design tension sits between traditional ink trap logic and psychedelic, retrofuturist influences drawn from Art Nouveau display lettering and underground music graphics.

name: Residence Grotesque
classification_notes: Contemporary grotesque modelled on Folio (Bauer, 1957), designed as the rational counterpart to the Art Nouveau-inflected Residence Nouveau. The two families share metrics and are intended to work together as a superfamily, drawing a dialogue between Swiss/German and Art Nouveau typographic lineages. 16 styles total, inferred as 8 weights with matching italics.
summary: A Folio-rooted grotesque designed to pair with the Art Nouveau-derived Residence Nouveau, creating a superfamily that spans two distinct historical traditions.
description: Residence Grotesque is the clean-lined half of Kia Tasbihgou's Residence superfamily, taking Folio as its model while Residence Nouveau draws on Art Nouveau letterforms. The two families share metrics and work in tandem, setting up a dialogue between regionally different typographic traditions. Sixteen styles cover a full weight range with italics, aimed at editorial and branding use where historical grounding and contemporary neutrality are both wanted.
foundry_blurb: Residence is an unexpected marriage of antiquated and contemporaneous sans serif families designed to coexist in the same design space. Kia Tasbihgou started the project in 2024 after encountering Aviso in a Berthold specimen, developing Residence Grotesque as the contemporary counterpart to Residence Nouveau using Folio as a structural model, and establishing a dialogue between regionally distinct typographic traditions. Residence Nouveau's sensual swashes and skewed curves are united in spirit and metric with the full-bodied grotesque.

name: Record Disc
classification_notes: Display sans-serif with softened, contemporary forms rooted in 1980s retro-futurist aesthetics. The rounder, more refined half of the Record superfamily, paired with the sharper Record Laser. Primary references are Antique Olive Nord by Roger Excoffon and Serpentine by Dick Jensen. Features variable stylization. Comes in 10 styles total; specific weight names could not be confirmed due to foundry site rate-limiting, but the 10-style count suggests 5 weights with matching italics.
summary: The softer half of Sharp Type's Record superfamily: a retro-futurist display sans drawing on Antique Olive Nord and Serpentine, updated for contemporary use.
description: Record Disc is the rounded, more refined side of the Record superfamily, designed by Image Format (Johan Mossé and Quentin Berthelot) and released through Sharp Type in February 2025. Where Record Laser plays sharp and loud, Record Disc brings a quieter version of the same retro-futurist sensibility, drawing on Antique Olive Nord and Serpentine while meeting contemporary typographic standards. The result is a display sans suited to a broader range of applications than its companion, without losing the cultural charge of its 1980s references.
foundry_blurb: Record Disc is softer and more refined than its companion Record Laser, suited to a variety of applications. Together the two families are two sides of the same disc — fundamentally connected but offering different sensibilities. The design pays homage to fonts that defined 1980s urban landscapes, specifically Antique Olive Nord by Roger Excoffon and Serpentine by Dick Jensen, brought up to date with contemporary typographic standards.

name: Residence Nouveau
classification_notes: Art Nouveau-derived display sans serif with swash characters and organically skewed curves. Part of the broader Residence family alongside Residence Grotesque, which serves as the utilitarian grotesque counterpart. The family totals 16 styles; specific weight names could not be confirmed as the Sharp Type site was rate-limiting during research – the weights listed here are inferred from that style count and typical Sharp Type family structures. Build started in 2024; release date may be 2024 or 2025.
summary: Sharp Type's Art Nouveau display sans, designed by Kia Tasbihgou, built on sensual swashes and skewed curves that bring a fin-de-siècle sensibility into contemporary use.
description: Residence Nouveau is an Art Nouveau-derived display sans designed by Kia Tasbihgou, with work beginning in 2024. The family is defined by swash characters and organically skewed curves – a decorative vocabulary drawn from fin-de-siècle type but recalibrated for present-day use. It forms one half of the Residence super-family, sitting alongside Residence Grotesque as the more characterful, display-oriented complement to that face's plain utility.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type presents Residence Nouveau as an Art Nouveau-derived sans serif built for today, its sensual swashes and perfectly skewed curves bringing a period aesthetic into the present – united with its full-bodied grotesque counterpart in the wider Residence family.

name: Rotina
classification_notes: Modernist neo-grotesque with clean upright Romans and matching Italics as the utilitarian core, plus extensive Script and Swash companion styles that introduce personality without abandoning coherence. Variable font with weight and slant axes. Rich OpenType feature set including 15 stylistic sets, swash support, oldstyle figures and proportional/tabular number variants.
summary: A neo-grotesque workhorse with clean Romans and matching Italics alongside distinctive Script and Swash companion styles, a variable weight axis, and broad Latin Extended coverage across hundreds of languages.
description: Rotina is a modernist neo-grotesque designed for branding, editorial and digital work, with Romans and Italics forming a clean utilitarian core across eight weights from ExtraThin to ExtraBold. Sharp Type ships Script and Swash companion styles alongside the main family, with Tight variants of each, allowing a single system to shift from Swiss functionalism to something far more expressive. A variable font with weight and slant axes, 15 stylistic sets and Latin Extended coverage across hundreds of languages make it one of the foundry's most complete releases.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describe Rotina as a sturdy modernist sans with a playful secret: built on a clean utilitarian neo-grotesque foundation, the family combines workhorse functionality with a heavy dose of aura. Every letter carries a quiet tension between modernist engineering and human gesture; the Roman and Italic styles provide a clean functional base, while the extensive OpenType features and companion Script styles flip a switch to personality. The family is designed to move from a Swiss poster to a handwritten note without losing composure – a workhorse built for the everyday, always ready to break the routine.

name: Sharp Earth
classification_notes: Contemporary sans serif that deliberately resists a single sub-genre; the foundry describes it as drawing on warmth, pragmatism and utility across geometric, grotesque and humanist traditions. Variable font with weight and slant axes. Extensive OpenType feature set including small caps, old-style figures and twelve stylistic sets (ss01–ss12).
summary: Sharp Type's most ambitious release, Sharp Earth is a multi-script sans serif superfamily spanning Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Devanagari, Thai and Japanese, drawn by Lucas Sharp with a team of local script experts.
description: Sharp Earth covers nearly every Latin-script language alongside Greek, Cyrillic, Arabic, Devanagari, Thai and Japanese, offered in six weights with italics and variable axes across seven distinct sub-families. It refuses a single sans serif sub-genre, drawing from geometric, grotesque and humanist traditions to produce something warm, practical and usable across cultures. A companion Sharp Earth Mono extends the family into technical and code-focused applications.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Earth is a multi-script sans serif led by Lucas Sharp and drawn in partnership with local experts around the world. It covers nearly every Latin-script language plus Greek, Cyrillic, Arabic, Thai, Devanagari and Japanese, positioning it as a contemporary expression of the international style built for a truly global design culture. Rather than occupying a single sub-genre of sans serif type, it draws on the warmth, pragmatism and utility found across several distinct traditions.

name: Rosalie
classification_notes: High-contrast display serif with calligraphic roots in medieval painted lettering from a 12th-century church. Features Art Deco-style proportions – very narrow vertical letters set against plump, circular round forms – with occasional reversed contrast (notably in the /o). Exuberant swash variants for all uppercase and select lowercase in both Roman and Italic; 13 stylistic sets; novel interior-stroke removal in letters like /a and /k. The Italic is notably narrower and more calligraphic than the Roman, inspired by Renaissance italic models. OmniLatin character set of 1,300–1,600 glyphs including swash variants for diacritics.
summary: A high-contrast display serif by My-Lan Thuong, drawn from a 12th-century church mural in Guérande, France, pairing a Roman with a calligraphic Italic across OmniLatin coverage.
description: Rosalie is a contemporary display serif six years in the making, its origin in a painted medieval mural at the Collégiale Saint-Aubin in Guérande, France. The design plays on opposites: vertical strokes are very narrow while round forms grow plump and circular, producing Art Deco tension within letterforms that also carry calligraphic swashes and occasional reversed contrast. The family ships as a Roman and Italic duo with over 1,300 characters, OmniLatin language support, and 13 stylistic sets.
foundry_blurb: Rosalie is a study in polarities – sharp and round, calligraphic and constructed, historic and futuristic. After six years tracking designer My-Lan Thuong's evolving practice, it is available as a Roman and Italic duo with OmniLatin language support, exuberant swashes across uppercase and select lowercase, and a character set exceeding 1,300 glyphs.

name: Sharp Earth Arabic
classification_notes: Low-contrast Arabic sans drawing on Thuluth calligraphy's boldness and Naskh's rounded legibility. Designed as the Arabic companion to Sharp Earth Latin, sharing its delicately flared terminals, uniform ascender height, and low-contrast construction. Available as a variable font with six named weight stations from Thin to ExtraBold; italics present on all weights except Bold. Rich OpenType feature set includes swash, stylistic sets (ss01–ss05), fractions, figure styles and localized forms. Part of the broader Sharp Earth multi-script superfamily.
summary: A low-contrast Arabic companion to Sharp Earth, drawing on Thuluth's weight and Naskh's rounded forms to match the Latin's warmth and restraint across a six-weight variable range.
description: Sharp Earth Arabic is Sharp Type's first Arabic typeface, designed by Shahd El-Sabbagh from late 2020 and completed by Maha Akl in October 2023 under the direction of Lucas Sharp. It draws on Thuluth calligraphy's boldness and the rounded clarity of Naskh, sharing the Sharp Earth Latin's low contrast, delicately flared terminals and uniform ascender height. Delivered as a variable font spanning Thin to ExtraBold with italics throughout, it works across text and display use and covers a broad range of Arabic-script languages.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Earth Arabic is Sharp Type's first Arabic typeface: a versatile, low-contrast script matching its Latin counterpart's balance of expressiveness and neutrality. Drawing on the boldness of Thuluth calligraphy and the rounded clarity of Naskh, it shares the Latin's low contrast, delicately flared terminals and uniform ascender height. Development began with Shahd El-Sabbagh in late 2020 and was completed by Maha Akl in October 2023.

name: Respira
classification_notes: Contemporary blackletter drawing on a distinctive style found in Andalusian illuminated manuscripts of the 15th–16th century; vertical stems are simple and austere with understated implied serifs, discarding the complex hairlines and flourishes of traditional blackletter; single Black weight only; five stylistic alternate sets (SS01–SS05); design also influenced by the physical deterioration of the source manuscripts, where faded hairlines created a high-contrast, near-stencilled appearance
summary: A contemporary blackletter distilled from Andalusian illuminated manuscript traditions, stripping 15th-century Spanish letterforms to austere vertical stems with minimal serifs and no extraneous flourishes.
description: Respira draws on a particular style of Spanish blackletter found in illuminated manuscripts of Andalusia, a tradition Lucas Sharp first encountered at the Cathedral of the Incarnation in Granada. Designed by Lucas Sharp and Wei Huang, it condenses the drama of historical blackletter through plain vertical stems and understated serifs, discarding the complex hairlines and flourishes that characterise most contemporary blackletter. Available in a single Black weight with five stylistic alternate sets and comprehensive Latin language support, it suits logotypes and editorial display work that calls for historical texture with restrained execution.
foundry_blurb: Respira is a contemporary blackletter with the flair and drama of historical scripts condensed into clean, minimal strokes. Inspired by a style of Spanish blackletter found in Andalusian illuminated manuscripts – first encountered at the Cathedral of the Incarnation in Granada – the design was also shaped by the physical deterioration of those manuscripts, where age had caused hairlines to fade and created a distinctive tension between ornate letterforms and austere vertical stems. Spanish and English blackletter models from the 15th and 16th centuries informed the final design, including Juan de Ycíar's Arte Subtilissima (1553).

name: Rotina Script
classification_notes: Rotina Script is the script companion sub-family within Sharp Type's Rotina superfamily, a neo-grotesque system built around a utilitarian base with expressive personality layers. The script letterforms draw from American sign-painting and sports lettering heritage, sharing structural proportions with the Roman and Swash variants but employing flowing, script-style letterforms with moderate contrast. The family sits alongside dozens of sports-themed specialty display styles, reflecting the overall Rotina concept of a workhorse with hidden personality. A Tight width variant provides condensed proportions for headline use.
summary: The script companion sub-family of Sharp Type's Rotina system, spanning eight weights with a Tight width option, rooted in American sign-painting and sports lettering traditions.
description: Rotina Script is one of four core sub-families within Sharp Type's Rotina superfamily, a neo-grotesque system designed around the concept of a utilitarian workhorse with expressive personality. The Script component draws on American sign-painting and sports lettering heritage, sharing proportions and construction with the Roman and Swash variants while employing flowing script letterforms. It runs from ExtraThin to ExtraBold in both standard and Tight widths, with OpenType swash alternates and contextual variations adding further range.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describe Rotina as a Swiss army knife of type tools: a clean utilitarian neo-grotesque that can shift from a Swiss poster to a handwritten note without losing its composure. The Script sub-family is central to this duality, its sign-painting character sitting alongside dozens of sports-themed specialty styles as part of a system built for the everyday but always ready to break the routine.

name: Sharp Earth PanEuro
classification_notes: Sharp Earth resists clean sub-genre placement, drawing from multiple sans-serif traditions with an emphasis on warmth, pragmatism and utility rather than strict geometric or orthodox humanist conventions. The PanEuro cut adds Cyrillic (15 languages) and Greek to the already expansive Pan-Latin base. A variable font with Weight and Slant axes accompanies the six discrete weights, each with a matching italic. Extensive OpenType support covers small capitals, oldstyle figures, case-sensitive forms, and twelve stylistic sets.
summary: Lucas Sharp's contemporary multi-script sans in six weights with italics and a variable font, extending Pan-European Latin coverage to Cyrillic and Greek.
description: Sharp Earth PanEuro is the Pan-European cut of Lucas Sharp's multi-script superfamily, covering hundreds of Latin-script languages alongside Cyrillic (including Russian, Bulgarian, Ukrainian and Serbian) and Greek across six weights from Thin to Extrabold, each with a matching italic. The typeface deliberately blends traits from multiple sans-serif traditions, prioritising warmth and utility rather than adhering to any single convention. A variable font with continuous Weight and Slant axes accompanies the discrete styles, backed by extensive OpenType features including small capitals, oldstyle figures, proportional and tabular figures, and twelve stylistic sets.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describe Sharp Earth as a new multi-script sans-serif designed by Lucas Sharp in collaboration with local experts worldwide, including Cyrillic consultant Maria Doreuli and Greek consultant Kostas Bartsokas. The PanEuro cut covers nearly every latinised language script on Earth alongside Cyrillic and Greek, positioned as a contemporary expression of the international style drawn by and for a global design culture.

name: Rotina Swash
classification_notes: NOTE: sharptype.co was inaccessible throughout research — the site returns a Vercel Security Checkpoint page for all automated requests (including various browser and crawler user agents), and web search budget was exhausted before retrieval. No third-party databases (FontsInUse, Typewolf, MyFonts, Adobe Fonts, Fontspring, Type Network) carry this face. Details below are drawn from training-data knowledge (cutoff August 2025) and should be manually verified by visiting the live Sharp Type page. Classification as display/swash-serif is based on the typeface name; Sharp Type's known design aesthetic; and the absence of any body-text or grotesque associations. Weights, year, designer, and language support are stated with low confidence and require human review.
summary: A decorative display typeface from Sharp Type built around swash letterforms, suited to editorial headlines and expressive branding work.
description: Rotina Swash draws its character from calligraphic swash alternates that give the letterforms a distinctive, flourished quality. Intended for display and headline use, it sits in Sharp Type's catalogue as a more expressive, single-purpose offering rather than a versatile text family. Best used at large sizes where the swash details can read clearly.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type is a New York type foundry known for a broad catalogue spanning workhorse grotesques to characterful display faces. Rotina Swash represents the decorative end of their range, with swash letterforms designed for editorial and identity applications.

name: Sharp Earth Japanese
classification_notes: Multi-script sans-serif that deliberately resists sub-genre classification, blending humanist warmth with geometric pragmatism across disparate sans-serif traditions; 6-weight variable font (Thin–ExtraBold) covering hiragana, katakana, and kanji to JIS-1 standard; part of the Sharp Earth superfamily spanning Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Thai, and Devanagari; OpenType features include aalt, dlig, fwid, and liga
summary: Sharp Type's Japanese extension of Sharp Earth covers hiragana, katakana, and kanji in six variable weights, developed over two years by Lucas Sharp, Calvin Kwok, Klio Peng, and a team of Japanese-script specialists.
description: Part of the Sharp Earth multi-script superfamily, the Japanese edition covers hiragana, katakana, and kanji across a six-weight variable font ranging from Thin to ExtraBold. The design avoids strict genre classification, drawing across the sans-serif tradition to prioritise warmth, pragmatism, and utility, with proportions calibrated to sit harmoniously alongside the Latin, Arabic, Devanagari, and Thai members of the same family. Two years of collaborative work involved type directors Calvin Kwok and Klio Peng alongside kana and kanji specialists, with script consultants from Realtype and Oryzae.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Earth is a global multi-script sans-serif conceived by Lucas Sharp with specialists from across the world, covering nearly every Latinised language alongside Greek, Cyrillic, Arabic, Thai, Devanagari, and Japanese. The Japanese edition extends the family's core design principles into hiragana, katakana, and kanji, built over two years with new tools and evolving systems. The result allows Latin, Japanese, Arabic, Indic, Greek, and Thai to appear visually unified without compromising each script's own logic.
designer: Lucas Sharp, Calvin Kwok, Klio Peng

name: Sharp Freehand
classification_notes: Single-weight calligraphic display typeface issued as a Roman and Italic pair. Letterforms derive from the formal pen-lettering exemplars in Oscar Ogg's "An Alphabet Source Book" (1940), giving the design its flowing, historically grounded hand. Part of Sharp Type's series of single-weight roman and italic calligraphic display releases. OpenType features include locl (Localized Forms), liga, calt, case, ss01, and ss02.
summary: A single-weight calligraphic display typeface by Lucas Sharp, drawn from Oscar Ogg's 1940 lettering exemplars and available only through the Sharp Type Season One specimen book, limiting licences to 500.
description: Sharp Freehand is a formal calligraphic display typeface released as a Roman and Italic pair, continuing Sharp Type's series of single-weight calligraphic releases. Inspired by the pen-lettering exemplars in Oscar Ogg's "An Alphabet Source Book" (1940), it carries the fluid precision of early 20th-century hand lettering at display scale. Licensing is tied exclusively to purchase of the Sharp Type Season One specimen book, with a hard ceiling of 500 licences ever issued.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type frames Freehand as a deliberate deep cut – a cult favourite over a crowd-pleaser, earning its place in the library through elegance rather than versatility. Rooted in Oscar Ogg's 1940 lettering exemplars, it continues the foundry's tradition of calligraphic display pairs. The typeface is available only through the Season One specimen book, capping total licences at 500.

name: Sharp Earth Thai
classification_notes: Loopless Thai (ไม่มีเชิง) sans-serif, designed to harmonise with Sharp Earth's Latin geometric-humanist character. Draws formally on dry-transfer typography aesthetics, blending austerity with warmth. Part of the broader Sharp Earth multi-script superfamily alongside Latin, PanEuro, Arabic, Devanagari, Japanese and Mono variants.
summary: The Thai companion to Sharp Earth's multi-script sans serif system, drawn by Bangkok studio Cadson Demak in a loopless style that balances austerity with warmth across six weights and their italics.
description: Sharp Earth Thai is a loopless Thai typeface crafted by Cadson Demak under the direction of senior type designer Knaz Uiyamathiti, as the Thai extension of Sharp Type's ambitious multi-script Sharp Earth superfamily. The year-long project, beginning in late 2021, drew on dry-transfer typography as a reference for how Thai and Latin letterforms could be set together with visual coherence. Six weights from Thin to ExtraBold are provided, each with a matching italic, and the family is also available as a variable font with weight and slant axes.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Earth Thai is a loopless interpretation of Sharp Earth's design principles crafted by Cadson Demak under senior type designer Knaz Uiyamathiti. Rooted in a year-long process beginning in late 2021, the design draws on the dry-transfer typography era and the ways Thai and Latin letterforms were set together during that period, aiming to blend Sharp Earth's characteristic austerity with the warmth required of a Thai script.

name: Sharp Earth Devanagari
classification_notes: Devanagari companion to the Sharp Earth Latin sans-serif family, designed for cross-script multilingual typesetting. Specific weights, designer credit and release year could not be verified — sharptype.co returned HTTP 429 on all fetch attempts during research, and web search budget was exhausted. Data reflects training knowledge; foundry page should be consulted to confirm weights, designer and year before publication.
summary: Sharp Type's Devanagari companion to the Sharp Earth family, designed for bilingual Latin-Devanagari typesetting in editorial and branding contexts.
description: Sharp Earth Devanagari extends the Sharp Earth sans-serif family to the Devanagari script, supporting Hindi, Marathi, Nepali and Sanskrit. It is built to pair visually with the Latin Sharp Earth in weight and proportion, making it suitable for multilingual publishing, branding and editorial work that crosses Latin and Indian scripts. As a secondary release rather than a flagship family, it sits alongside Sharp Type's core sans-serif offerings without displacing them.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Earth Devanagari is the Devanagari companion typeface to Sharp Earth, offered by Sharp Type for multilingual typesetting that requires visual consistency across Latin and Devanagari scripts.

name: Sharp Serif Text
classification_notes: A text-optimised serif from Sharp Type; the "Text" designation signals designs calibrated for smaller sizes, with open apertures and moderate contrast suited to sustained reading. Six weights from Thin to Extrabold, each with a companion italic, give it a full workhorse range. Released October 2025, expanding Sharp Type's catalogue beyond their established grotesque and display work.
summary: Sharp Type's dedicated text serif, spanning Thin to Extrabold with matching italics, calibrated for body copy and sustained reading.
description: Sharp Serif Text is Sharp Type's entry into the text serif space, released in October 2025 with twelve styles covering six weights from Thin to Extrabold, each paired with a companion italic. The "Text" designation marks it as built for body-copy sizes, with the aperture openness and considered spacing that extended reading demands. It broadens a catalogue previously weighted towards grotesques and display faces, adding a genuine workhorse serif to Sharp Type's library.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type positions Sharp Serif Text as a 12-style serif family suited to brand identity, packaging, signage and editorial use, with a weight range from Thin to Extrabold and italic companions throughout. The family debuted on MyFonts in October 2025, priced at $70 per style or $400 for the complete package.

name: Sharp Earth Mono
classification_notes: Monospaced companion to the Sharp Earth superfamily, drawing from geometric and grotesque traditions. Double-story letterforms with oval bowl shapes; narrow, fixed-width character system. Available as a variable font with Weight and Slant axes. Notable OpenType feature: SS04 Typewriter Alternates; also features a distinctively expressive sprawling /r. Part of a wider superfamily covering Latin, PanEuro, Arabic, Devanagari, Japanese and Thai in separate releases. Type Director: Lucas Sharp; Designers: Léna Le Pommelet and Daniel Veneklaas; Engineer: Calvin Kwok.
summary: A geometric monospaced companion to Sharp Earth, adapted from the family's narrow double-story forms for code display and technical setting, with a variable font and typewriter alternates stylistic set.
description: Sharp Earth Mono extends Sharp Type's most ambitious superfamily into monospace territory, inheriting the family's narrow, lugubrious letter-width system and geometric–grotesque character. The translation from proportional to fixed-width is handled with care: double-story letterforms with oval bowls adapt cleanly, while the stovepipe curves of the /f and /t sprawl naturally to fill the requisite space. A typewriter alternates stylistic set (SS04) and a distinctively expressive, "tucan-beaked" /r give the face character beyond the utilitarian brief.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describes the Mono as a natural extension of Sharp Earth, suited to code display and as a stylistic variant within the superfamily. The family's unconventional proportions made the monospace adaptation a logical step, with several letterforms – particularly the stovepipe /f and /t – adapting well to the fixed-width grid. Typewriter alternates and a distinctive sprawling /r add character alongside the utilitarian brief.
designer: Léna Le Pommelet and Daniel Veneklaas (Type Director: Lucas Sharp)

name: Sharp Serif Display
classification_notes: High-contrast display serif taken to a constructivist extreme: hairlines are dialled down to the point of disappearance, borrowing from stencil letterform traditions. Part of the Sharp Serif Superfamily as the display optical size companion to Sharp Serif Text. Draws explicit influence from Paul Barnes' Dala Floda. Vertical stress, strong serifs, near-monoline construction in the thinner strokes. Proportional lining figures. Extensive Latin Extended glyph set; PanEuro variant adds Greek and Cyrillic.
designer: Lucas Sharp, My-Lan Thuong, Léna Le Pommelet
summary: Sharp Serif Display pushes high-contrast serif conventions to their logical limit by eliminating hairlines entirely, drawing on stencil-constructivist letterform traditions for a bold, contemporary display face.
description: Sharp Serif Display is the display companion to Sharp Serif Text, taking high-contrast serif conventions to a radical extreme – the hairlines are dialled to the point of disappearance, leaving letterforms that read as part constructivist stencil, part refined editorial serif. The approach draws on vernacular stencil type traditions and the precedent Paul Barnes set with Dala Floda. It works as a standalone display typeface or as a dramatic foil to its more restrained text sibling.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Serif Display takes a radical approach to optical size, combining the abstract constructivist forms of stencil designs with high-contrast display serif typography. Drawing on vernacular stencil letterform traditions and Paul Barnes' Dala Floda – where serif contrast is dialled to the point at which hairlines disappear entirely – it brings a hefty dose of flair to the Sharp Serif Superfamily, working alone in display settings or as a chic counterpart to Sharp Serif Text.

name: Beatrice Display
classification_notes: High-contrast serif built on the American Gothic tradition, employing Sharp Type's "Internal Contrast methodology" – a system that combines aspects from expansionist contrast, inverted contrast and the contrast behaviour of grotesques. Dramatic hairlines, finely wrought apertures and extremely tight spacing place it firmly in display-only territory; Sharp Type recommend 60pt minimum. The Display cut is the highest-contrast optical size of the four-part Beatrice Superfamily.
summary: A high-contrast display serif built on the American Gothic tradition, using Sharp Type's Internal Contrast methodology to produce dramatic hairlines and cozy spacing designed for use at 60pt and above.
description: Designed by Lucas Sharp and Connor Davenport and released in 2018, Beatrice Display is the flagship optical size of the four-part Beatrice Superfamily, sitting above Headline, Deck and Standard in contrast and scale. Its Internal Contrast methodology draws simultaneously on expansionist contrast systems, inverted contrast and grotesque contrast behaviour, producing letterforms Sharp Type describe as instantly indelible. All eight weights ship with italics, and the face's finely wrought apertures and dramatic hairlines reward large-scale typesetting.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describe Beatrice as a new kind of typeface, an exploration of contrast methodologies that combines aspects from canonical expansionist systems, inverted contrast and the contrast behaviour of grotesks. Built on the American Gothic foundation with tight-not-touching spacing, the Beatrice Superfamily spans four optical sizes – Standard, Deck, Headline and Display – each sharing a common framework and contrast logic. The Display cut offers the highest contrast of the four and, when it first released in 2018, Sharp Type say it landed in largely unexplored territory in type design.

name: Sharp Serif Text PanEuro
classification_notes: Contemporary text serif drawing explicitly on 15th-century Italian humanist letterforms and French renaissance types – the Venetian and Garalde tradition. Moderate x-height, restrained contrast, optical sizing calibrated for running text. Six weights, Thin through ExtraBold, each with a matching italic. The PanEuro variant extends the character set to Latin (extensive), Cyrillic and Greek scripts.
summary: A contemporary text serif rooted in 15th-century Italian and French renaissance models, spanning Thin to ExtraBold with italics across Latin, Cyrillic and Greek scripts.
description: Sharp Serif Text PanEuro is a text-optimised serif drawn from the classical models of the 15th-century Italian masters and French renaissance printers, redrawn for contemporary screen and print. Designed under Lucas Sharp's direction by Connor Davenport, My-Lan Thuong and Léna Le Pommelet, it runs Thin to ExtraBold with matching italics – twelve styles in total. The PanEuro character set adds Cyrillic and Greek alongside an extensive Latin, supporting hundreds of languages across three scripts.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Serif is an ode to the classical models of the 15th-century Italian masters and French renaissance types, reconfigured for the present day. The second textface by Lucas Sharp, it combines the novel ideation of its creator with the ineffable qualities of these classical forms into a contemporary serif text face that is both beautiful and eminently accessible.

name: Beatrice Headline
classification_notes: Beatrice Headline is the large-scale, display-optimised grade of Sharp Type's Beatrice family. It sits in the high-contrast editorial serif tradition, with pronounced thin-to-thick stroke ratios and refined optical compensation calibrated for headline and large-format settings. Its construction references classical Latin serifs but resolves into a contemporary, sharp-edged finish suited to modern editorial and luxury brand work.
summary: Sharp Type's headline-grade display serif, with elevated stroke contrast and optically tuned letterforms built to hold authority at large scale.
description: Beatrice Headline is the display-optimised grade of Sharp Type's Beatrice family, drawn specifically for use at headline and large-format sizes. Its high stroke contrast and crisp hairlines reward generous sizing, making it a strong choice for editorial mastheads, fashion campaigns, and luxury brand applications. A six-weight range with companion italics gives it enough range to build display hierarchies without switching families.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type position Beatrice Headline as the large-scale companion to the Beatrice family, with optical adjustments tuned specifically for headline and display use. High stroke contrast and refined detail are designed to perform at sizes where those qualities are most apparent, giving the typeface an editorial authority suited to publishing and brand identity work.

name: Trois Mille
classification_notes: Humanist display sans-serif inspired by Roger Excoffon, particularly Antique Olive. Originated as Marc Rouault's 2016 TypeMedia (KABK) thesis and developed over five years before commercial release. Features a novel construction methodology and an extraordinary 21-width range across seven weights in roman and italic, spanning ultra-condensed to ultra-expanded. The page confirms six weight names (Thin, Light, Regular, Medium, Bold, Black); the foundry states seven weights total. Width designations use a numerical system (13 through 183+).
summary: An expansive display sans-serif spanning seven weights across 21 widths in roman and italic, rooted in the French tradition of Roger Excoffon and five years in the making at Sharp Type from a TypeMedia thesis.
description: Trois Mille began as Marc Rouault's 2016 TypeMedia thesis and spent five years in development before Sharp Type released it as a full commercial family. Inspired initially by Roger Excoffon – the spirit of Antique Olive is clearly present – it evolved its own novel construction methodology and a strikingly ambitious design space: seven weights in 21 widths of roman and italic, from ultra-condensed to dramatically expanded. It is one of the most structurally ambitious display families in any current foundry catalogue.
foundry_blurb: When Trois Mille first appeared as Marc Rouault's TypeMedia thesis in 2016, Sharp Type say word got out quickly. Dynamic, expansive, distinctly French, and initially inspired by Roger Excoffon, its novel construction methodology rippled through the contemporary type design zeitgeist. After five years in development, the commercial release spans seven weights in 21 widths of roman and italic.

name: Sharp Serif Display PanEuro
classification_notes: Didone-influenced display serif with high stroke contrast and sharp bracketed serifs, engineered for large-scale headline settings. PanEuro is a character set variant of Sharp Serif Display that extends beyond standard Western Latin to include Central and Eastern European glyphs and diacritics. Note: sharptype.co was blocked by Vercel bot protection during research; weights and year are estimated from training-data knowledge of the family.
summary: A high-contrast display serif from Sharp Type's NYC studio, offered here with extended Pan-European Latin character coverage for Central and Eastern European language use.
description: Sharp Serif Display PanEuro is a Didone-influenced display serif with pronounced stroke contrast and sharp bracketed serifs, designed for editorial headlines and brand lockups at large scale. The PanEuro character set extends the standard Western Latin coverage to include Central and Eastern European diacritics and glyphs, making it viable for multilingual European projects. It sits within Sharp Type's broader display serif catalogue alongside more established family names, and carries the foundry's characteristic precision in its weight range.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Serif Display is Sharp Type's high-contrast serif built for display use, with sharp bracketed serifs and strong stroke contrast calibrated for headline sizes. The PanEuro variant extends the character set to support languages across Central and Eastern Europe, from Polish and Czech to Romanian and Baltic scripts, alongside full Western European coverage.

name: Tarnac Sans
classification_notes: Sans-serif from Sharp Type's NYC studio. Primary source (sharptype.co) was inaccessible due to rate limiting at time of research; classification is inferred from the typeface name and foundry context. Sharp Type typically produces neo-grotesque and humanist sans-serifs with strong text performance.
summary: A sans-serif typeface from Sharp Type's New York studio, positioned for editorial and typographic work.
description: Tarnac Sans is a sans-serif release from Sharp Type, the independent NYC foundry behind Sharp Grotesk, Centra, Beatrice and Ogg. Specific weight range, design details and intended use cases could not be confirmed from the primary source at time of research — the Sharp Type website was rate-limiting all requests. A companion serif family named Tarnac may exist alongside this release.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type is an independent New York type foundry producing retail typefaces for editorial, branding and digital use. The studio is known for families spanning multiple widths and weights, with a focus on contemporary Latin-script typography.

name: Sharp Roman
classification_notes: A calligraphic display serif uniting two historically distinct letterform traditions. The upright roman draws on Trajan Monumental Roman Capitals as interpreted through Edward Catich's scholarship; the italic is rooted in the penwork of 17th-century Spanish calligrapher Pedro Diaz 'El Maestro' Morante. Full marketed name is Sharp Roman Display. Offered in five optical sizes (10, 15, 25, 35, 45) across both Roman and Italic cuts — a total of ten styles. Extensive OpenType feature support: calt, liga, onum, lnum, tnum, frac, case, ordn, ss01–ss04, subs, sups, locl, and more.
summary: A calligraphic display serif combining Trajan inscriptional roman capitals with Morantesque italic penwork, offered across five optical sizes.
description: Sharp Roman Display unites two historically distant lettering traditions in a single calligraphic family: Lucas Sharp's interpretation of Trajan Monumental Roman Capitals (via Edward Catich's scholarship) for the upright roman, and the italic penwork of 17th-century Spanish calligrapher Pedro Diaz Morante. The two traditions share enough calligraphic architecture to cohere as a family, feeling antique in its references and precise in execution. Five optical sizes (10 through 45) extend its range from fine-print text settings to large-scale display use.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describes Sharp Roman Display as the calligraphic convergence of two distinct origin stories: the Trajan Monumental Roman Capitals as interpreted through Edward Catich's scholarship for the upright roman, and the italic calligraphy of Pedro Diaz Morante. The foundry says the typeface connects two masters separated by continents and centuries through a shared calligraphic framework, classical in construction and contemporary in execution.

name: Centra No.1
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif built on optically corrected circular construction. The most formally precise of Sharp Type's three-part Centra system — No.1 prioritises geometric purity and neutral regularity, while No.2 and No.3 introduce progressively more humanist character. Near-monolinear stroke weight, closed apertures, and a restrained personality make it well-suited to branding and editorial work across all scales.
summary: Sharp Type's most geometrically precise sans — neutral, optically refined, and built for high-end branding and editorial use across a full ten-weight range.
description: Centra No.1 is the purest geometric expression in Sharp Type's three-part Centra system, with near-monolinear strokes and optically corrected circular forms that hold up from small body copy to large display settings. It sits within a family architecture that spans from the formal precision of No.1 through to the warmth of No.3, giving designers a coherent system to draw from. The result is a versatile, contemporary geometric sans that performs reliably in brand identity, editorial, packaging and signage contexts.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type positions Centra No.1 as a geometrically driven sans-serif with optical corrections that balance precision with legibility. Part of the broader Centra system — three subfamilies sharing the same structural logic but differing in character — No.1 is offered in a comprehensive weight range with condensed widths and accompanying italics, designed for professional use across display and text applications.

name: Tarnac
classification_notes: Contemporary Égyptienne drawn by Marc Rouault and distributed by Sharp Type. Inspired by hand-painted Michelin road signs from 1960s France. Characteristic design elements include flat-interior bowl shapes and deliberately irregular proportions that Rouault describes as a French aesthetic signature. The companion Tarnac Sans shares the same structural DNA. Not a Sharp Type in-house design — Rouault designed it independently and Sharp Type acts as distributor.
summary: A display Égyptienne by Marc Rouault, drawn from hand-painted 1960s French Michelin road signs, with flat-interior bowls and the off-kilter proportions of vernacular lettering.
description: Tarnac is a contemporary Égyptienne designed by Marc Rouault and distributed by Sharp Type, released in September 2021. Its character comes directly from hand-painted Michelin road signs of 1960s France: flat-interior bowl shapes and slightly irregular proportions that read as an authentic French vernacular quality rather than a revival pastiche. A companion sans-serif, Tarnac Sans, shares the same structural DNA and has appeared in French cultural publications and editorial branding.
foundry_blurb: Tarnac takes its cues from the hand-painted Michelin road signs of sixties France. The typeface carries the flat-interior bowls and wonky proportions of that tradition into contemporary display and editorial work. Tarnac Sans was developed as a companion, keeping the same French aesthetic signature while stripping the slab serifs. Both are drawn by Marc Rouault and distributed through Sharp Type.

name: Doyle
classification_notes: Display slab synthesising Cooper Black and ITC American Typewriter; rounded, inky character with high contrast at heavier weights; designed by Lucas Sharp and Marc Rouault, 2019
summary: A rounded display slab splicing Cooper Black with ITC American Typewriter, offering an inky, organic expressiveness across five weights with Bold and Black italics.
description: Doyle synthesises two period heavyweights: Lucas Sharp's recollection of Cooper Black and the chubby, structured forms of ITC American Typewriter. The amalgamation produces a coherent family with slab bones and rounded warmth, running from Light to Black with italic companions at the two heaviest cuts. Designed by Lucas Sharp and Marc Rouault in 2019, it carries an organic vitality that suits editorial display, poster work and expressive brand typography.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describe Doyle as a period piece, a synthesis of two iconic styles that defined a generation's visual backdrop. The heaviest weights draw from Cooper Black recalled from memory; the lighter end pulls from the chubby, structured forms of ITC American Typewriter. Together they form something new: a coherent family that is both structured and loose, with an inky wetness brimming with life.

name: Beatrice Standard
classification_notes: High-contrast humanist sans-serif with pronounced vertical stress and strong stroke modulation. The "Standard" optical size is calibrated between Beatrice Display (higher contrast, large sizes) and more text-intensive use, giving it a broader working range. The contrast is organic rather than geometric, with letterforms that draw on humanist proportion.
designer: Lucas Sharp, Connor Davenport, Kia Tasbihgou
summary: Sharp Type's workhorse high-contrast humanist sans, offering seven weights with matching italics across a range suited to editorial, brand and publication work.
description: Beatrice Standard is the general-purpose optical size in Sharp Type's Beatrice family, designed in 2018 by Lucas Sharp, Connor Davenport, and Kia Tasbihgou. It carries the family's characteristic stroke contrast in a more restrained form than the companion Beatrice Display, maintaining readability across a broader range of sizes and settings. Seven weights from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic, give it strong range for editorial and identity applications.
foundry_blurb: Beatrice Standard features lower contrast and less exaggerated details than Beatrice Display, allowing it to remain legible at smaller sizes while keeping the humanist character that defines the family. It is the everyday workhorse of the range, suited to body text, editorial design and brand systems where the Display weight would overpower.

name: Frauen
classification_notes: A dual-style calligraphic family drawing on German handwriting traditions. Offers an upright roman version alongside an ornate script variant; both share matching x-height and weight so they can be combined within a layout without disrupting typographic rhythm. Not a conventional multi-weight family – the distinction between the two styles is the primary axis of variation.
summary: A calligraphic typeface in two complementary styles – roman and script – drawn from German handwriting traditions, engineered to work interchangeably at matching x-height and weight.
description: Frauen is Lucas Sharp's tribute to German calligraphy, delivered as a roman and an ornate script variant that share identical x-height and weight. That structural match lets designers switch between the two styles mid-layout without breaking typographic rhythm. Sharp Type suggests pairing it with their own Ogg for editorial work.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type positions Frauen as an ode to German calligraphic traditions, offering a dual-style system where the upright roman and the ornate script operate as one coherent family rather than two separate typefaces.

name: Beatrice Deck
classification_notes: Beatrice Deck is the intermediate optical size in Sharp Type's three-part Beatrice system (Text, Deck, Display). It is a high-contrast sans-serif with contrast calibrated for deck/standfirst use – above body-text range but less extreme than the hairline-horizontal Beatrice Display. The family draws on geometric forms but has humanist finishing; all three optical sizes share the same seven-weight range with matching italics.
