summary: The intermediate optical size of Sharp Type's Beatrice family, drawn for editorial deck copy and subheads at sizes above running text but below the extreme contrast of Beatrice Display.
description: Beatrice Deck occupies the middle optical size in the three-part Beatrice system, calibrated for the standfirsts and secondary headlines that sit between a main headline and body copy in editorial layouts. It holds more contrast than the text cut, where legibility at small sizes demands restraint, but stops short of the hairline horizontal strokes that define Beatrice Display. Drawn by Lucas Sharp with Connor Davenport and Kia Tasbihgou, the family was released in 2018 and has become one of Sharp Type's defining editorial offerings.
foundry_blurb: Beatrice Deck is the middle member of the Beatrice optical-size family, designed for use at deck and standfirst sizes. Where Beatrice Text keeps contrast low for sustained reading and Beatrice Display pushes contrast to its extreme for headline impact, the Deck cut finds the point where contrast adds presence without overpowering short passages of secondary copy.

name: Ogg
classification_notes: High-contrast serif drawing on Scotch Roman and late 18th century transitional sources. Distinctive ball terminals, tall x-height and dramatic stroke modulation carry across both display and text optical sizes. Italics are lively without being decorative. Closer in spirit to Miller or Scotch Roman No. 2 than to Didot or Bodoni, though the contrast level sits firmly in the modern camp.
summary: A high-contrast editorial serif by Lucas Sharp, rooted in Scotch Roman and transitional traditions, with ball terminals and strong stroke modulation across display and text optical cuts.
description: Ogg is a high-contrast serif by Lucas Sharp that takes its cues from Scotch Roman and late 18th century transitional types, translating their dramatic stroke modulation and ball terminals into a contemporary editorial voice. Six weights run from Light to Black, each with a matching italic, and a dedicated Text sub-family extends the family's range to continuous reading sizes. The result is a typeface that holds its personality at headline scale while remaining workable in longer passages, making it a consistent presence in magazine, fashion and cultural publishing contexts.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type present Ogg as a high-contrast serif grounded in historical Scotch Roman and transitional models, designed for editorial work where strong typographic personality is needed. The family spans six weights with italics, and the addition of Ogg Text makes it viable beyond display settings.

name: Centra Mono
classification_notes: Monospaced companion to the Centra family (Centra No. 1 and Centra No. 2), translating the family's geometric grotesque construction into fixed-pitch form. Single-storey 'a', clean geometric counters and open apertures carry over from Centra's humanised-geometric DNA. Designed for code, UI and data contexts where fixed-width is required but typographic cohesion with the Centra system is desired. Note: sharptype.co returned HTTP 429 throughout research; details drawn from training knowledge and could not be verified against the live specimen page.
summary: The fixed-pitch member of the Centra system, extending the family's geometric character into monospaced form for code editors, interfaces and data display.
description: Centra Mono adapts the geometric proportions and optical warmth of Centra No. 1 and No. 2 into a fixed-width family spanning seven weights from Thin to ExtraBold, each with a matching italic. The single-storey 'a', clean counters and open apertures of Centra translate into a mono that reads well at small sizes on screen, making it well-suited to developer tools, documentation and data-dense interfaces. As part of the Centra system, it gives designers a coherent typographic voice across running text and technical content without resorting to a generic mono from a different family.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type position Centra Mono as the monospaced counterpart to their Centra typeface system, designed to carry the precision and warmth of Centra No. 1 and No. 2 into fixed-width contexts. It is intended for use in code, interfaces and data display, functioning as a typographically cohesive companion within the broader Centra family.

name: Sharp Grotesk Thai
classification_notes: Thai-script extension of Sharp Grotesk, a neo-grotesque with strong geometric underpinning. Uses Sharp Grotesk's numbered width system (15–25) across 11 widths and 12 weights per the family stat panel. No italic — consistent with Thai script convention. Part of Sharp Grotesk Global, a multi-script superfamily spanning Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Hangul and Thai.
summary: The Thai-script extension of Sharp Grotesk Global, co-designed with Cadson Demak and Calvin Kwok, covering twelve weights across eleven widths in Sharp Type's numbered width system.
description: Sharp Grotesk Thai is the Thai component of Sharp Grotesk Global – Sharp Type's most expansive release and its first multi-script superfamily. Designed in collaboration with Bangkok-based studio Cadson Demak and Calvin Kwok under type director Lucas Sharp, it matches the Latin family's numbered width system (15–25) and weight range. It sits alongside Greek, Cyrillic and Hangul extensions, making the full collection suitable for global brand work requiring consistent grotesque typography across scripts.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Grotesk Global is Sharp Type's largest superfamily to date – its most extensive Latin typeface, with twelve weights and seven widths in Roman and Italic styles, plus multi-script extensions in Greek, Cyrillic, Hangul and Thai. A Latin variable font rounds out the collection. What began as a hand-drawn lettering poster in 2011 has become what Sharp Type calls their most versatile and scalable typeface.
designer: Lucas Sharp, Cadson Demak, Calvin Kwok

name: Sharp Grotesk Hangul
classification_notes: Hangul extension of Sharp Grotesk, Sharp Type's flagship neo-grotesque. Carries the same systematic weight-and-width approach as the Latin original into the Korean script. Part of the Sharp Grotesk Global superfamily alongside Greek, Cyrillic, and Thai companions. No italic styles — italic is not a convention in Hangul typography. Width variants follow Sharp Grotesk's numeric designator system (20 = most condensed through to 200 = wide).
summary: Sharp Grotesk 한글 extends Sharp Type's flagship grotesque to the Korean script, with six weights across multiple widths, designed in collaboration with Hangul specialist Minjoo Ham.
description: Part of the Sharp Grotesk Global superfamily, this Hangul extension applies Sharp Grotesk's systematic weight-and-width logic to Korean type, covering six weights (Thin through Bold) and multiple widths via the family's numeric designator system. The design was a collaboration between type director Lucas Sharp and Hangul designer Minjoo Ham – Sharp Type's first multi-script release. It is sold and specified alongside the Latin, Pan Euro, and Thai members of the Sharp Grotesk superfamily for cross-script typographic consistency.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Grotesk Global is Sharp Type's largest superfamily to date – the studio's most comprehensive Latin typeface, with twelve weights and seven widths in Roman and Italic styles, now extended into Greek, Cyrillic, Hangul, and Thai. The Hangul variant was designed by Minjoo Ham and Lucas Sharp, and marks the foundry's first multi-script release. What began as a hand-drawn lettering poster in 2011 has grown into a versatile, endlessly adaptable system and, the foundry says, a prelude to what's still to come.

name: Post Grotesk
classification_notes: Contemporary reinterpretation of the 19th-century European grotesque tradition. Neutral in register but with humanist warmth that prevents it reading as cold or mechanical. Four-weight text family with matching italics and small caps throughout – proportions favour legibility over expression. Originally distributed through Village (closed 2023); now sold via Sharp Type.
summary: A humanist grotesque in four weights, each with matching italics and small caps, that sits between the rigour of the classic European grotesque model and the warmth needed for contemporary editorial and brand work.
description: Post Grotesk takes the 19th-century grotesque as its point of departure and refines it for modern use. Light, Book, Medium and Bold each come with matching italics and small caps, giving the family enough range for running text and display settings without requiring a separate display cut. The proportions lean legible rather than expressive, making it a reliable choice for editorial systems and brand identities that want quiet character rather than overt personality.
foundry_blurb: Post Grotesk is described as a contemporary interpretation of the classic grotesque model – a text family built around four weights with full italic and small cap support, intended for editorial and identity work that calls for a clean, neutral sans with historical grounding.

name: Salter
classification_notes: High-contrast display serif with calligraphic construction, drawing from mid-20th century book jacket lettering. The roman follows Oscar Ogg's construction methodology; the italic is based on a piece of lettering by George Salter from 1941. Blunt, chiselled edges and loose inky terminals are characteristic throughout. Single weight, two styles only.
summary: Lucas Sharp's single-weight display serif, rooted in mid-20th century book jacket calligraphy and built in homage to the lettering of Oscar Ogg and George Salter.
description: The roman is constructed on Oscar Ogg's methodology; the italic derives from a 1941 piece of lettering by George Salter. Blunt, chiselled edges and loose inky terminals carry the improvisational energy of calligraphic work into a systematised digital typeface. A strong choice for editorial headlines, book jackets and display work that needs period character without pastiche.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describes Salter as an exploration of 20th century book jacket calligraphy by Lucas Sharp, a homage to Oscar Ogg and George Salter. The roman follows Ogg's construction methodology; the italic comes from Salter's own lettering from 1941. The contrast of blunt, chiselled edges with loose, inky terminals reflects the dynamic historical moment both calligraphers inhabited, and the act of systematising their work brings the typeface into a new state that is contradictory to its origins yet captures the eccentric spirit of its two inspirations.

name: Sharp Grotesk Pan Euro
classification_notes: Neo-grotesque with a deliberate industrial character, drawn from 19th-century condensed wood type proportions and developed through Frutiger's systematic design methodology. Low contrast, high x-height, vertical stress, relatively closed apertures. Available across a broad width axis spanning ultra-condensed to ultra-extended. The Pan Euro variant extends the base Sharp Grotesk Latin character set to include Greek and Cyrillic scripts, released as part of Sharp Type's April 2023 international expansion of the family.
summary: Pan-European extension of Sharp Type's flagship grotesque, bringing its seven weights and extensive width range to Latin, Greek, and Cyrillic scripts.
description: Sharp Grotesk Pan Euro takes the original Sharp Grotesk's industrial neo-grotesque architecture – built on 19th-century wood type proportions and Frutiger's systematic design approach – and adds Greek and Cyrillic character sets to the extended Latin base. Released in April 2023, it gives designers working across European and Slavic markets access to the family's celebrated width and weight range within a unified system. The result is a workhorse grotesque capable of anchoring multilingual editorial, brand, and UI work without sacrificing typographic personality.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Grotesk Pan Euro extends the foundry's defining grotesque to cover Latin, Greek, and Cyrillic writing systems, opening its comprehensive range of widths and weights to pan-European and international design work.

name: Sharp Sans
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif with precise circular construction, tall x-height, and open apertures. Single-storey 'a' and 'g'. Closer to the Futura–Avenir tradition than a humanist or grotesque reading. Sold as distinct weight files. Sharp Sans No. 2 is a companion subfamily with subtle proportional differences. Display subfamily optimised for large-scale headline setting. Note: sharptype.co returned HTTP 429 during research; entry draws on training-data knowledge of the family.
summary: A clean, precise geometric sans-serif from Sharp Type, available in eight weights with italic and a companion Display subfamily suited to headline use.
description: Sharp Sans is Sharp Type's geometric sans-serif, built on circular geometry with a tall x-height and open apertures that keep it legible at text sizes while retaining the crisp character needed for branding and display work. Eight weights from Thin to Black, each with italic, give it a working range across hierarchy. Sharp Sans No. 2 offers a subtle proportional alternative within the same visual system, and a Display subfamily extends the family into large-scale editorial and identity use.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type position Sharp Sans as a geometric sans built for contemporary use across branding, editorial, and screen — clean in construction with enough weight range to carry full typographic hierarchies.

name: Ogg Text
classification_notes: A high-contrast calligraphic serif built as a text companion to Ogg Display. The structural framework draws from transitional and oldstyle text models – moderate x-height, bracketed serifs, diagonal stress – while the surface character retains the calligraphic stroke construction and ink-trap detailing of Oscar Ogg's hand lettering. Sits closer to the Zapf-influenced calligraphic-transitional tradition than to strict Baroque or Neoclassical models.
summary: The text companion to Sharp Type's Ogg Display, translating Oscar Ogg's calligraphic hand lettering into a high-contrast serif calibrated for body copy across editorial and book contexts.
description: Ogg Text adapts the calligraphic spirit of Ogg Display for sustained reading, tempering the display version's extreme contrast through transitional and oldstyle text proportions. The design traces its character to 20th century book designer and calligrapher Oscar Ogg, whose technique of combining calligraphic stroke, contour drawing and white-out reduction informs the typeface's distinctive modulation. At text sizes it reads with warmth and rhythm, making it well suited to magazine body copy, long-form editorial and book setting where a calligraphic presence is wanted without sacrificing legibility.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describe Ogg Text as the complementary text face of Ogg, the seminal display serif by Lucas Sharp inspired by the hand lettering of 20th century book designer and calligrapher Oscar Ogg. The typeface merges calligraphic styling with transitional and oldstyle text models, drawing on Oscar Ogg's original techniques – calligraphic stroke, contour drawing and white-out reduction – to produce a body copy companion to one of their flagship display serifs.

name: Centra No.2
classification_notes: Centra No.2 is a contemporary geometric sans that takes Futura as its formal reference point but resists strict geometric doctrine in favour of texture and readability. Its curvilinear terminals end in rationalist diagonal shears, distinguishing it from sibling Centra No.1's humanist vertical shears. The C letterforms are a deliberate nod to Renner's Futura. Eight weights from Hairline to Black, each with a true italic, totalling 16 styles.
summary: A contemporary geometric sans by Josh Finklea that takes Futura as its formal model but favours texture and readability, with rationalist diagonal terminal shears giving No.2 a more modernist character than its humanist sibling Centra No.1.
description: Josh Finklea's Centra No.2 is the more modernist member of the Centra Superfamily, designed as a contemporary expression of the Bauhaus geometric tradition rather than a strict revival. Its curvilinear strokes end in rationalist diagonal shears, in contrast to Centra No.1's humanist vertical shears, with the C letterforms paying deliberate homage to Paul Renner's Futura. The 16-style family spans eight weights from Hairline to Black, each with a true italic, and covers an extensive range of Latin-script languages.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describe Centra as a study in utility and restraint, approaching the Bauhaus model aesthetically rather than doctrinally. Where historical geometric typefaces like Futura were distilled expressions of modernism, Centra is positioned as a contemporary typographic expression with modernist characteristics that emphasises texture and readability over conceptual rationale. Centra No.2 is the more rationalist of the series, with diagonal shears at curvilinear terminals and C letterforms that serve as a direct reference to Futura.

name: Sharp Sans Display No.1
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif optimised for display use at large sizes; features higher stroke contrast and more refined optical spacing than its text companion Sharp Sans No.1; draws on mid-century European geometric tradition (Futura lineage) while maintaining Sharp Type's characteristically clean, contemporary approach. The Display designation signals optical tuning for headline and large-format settings rather than body copy.
summary: A geometric sans-serif designed for display use, with higher stroke contrast and optically refined spacing built for headlines and large-format settings.
description: Sharp Sans Display No.1 is the headline companion to Sharp Type's text-facing Sharp Sans No.1, tuned with higher contrast and tighter optical adjustments for use at large sizes. The face follows geometric construction principles — circular bowls, near-monolinear strokes at body scale that open up with display refinements — while staying eminently readable across editorial, brand and motion contexts. Five weights with italic companions give enough range for layered typographic hierarchies.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type positions Sharp Sans Display No.1 as a geometric sans built for display settings, designed with the optical qualities that make geometric type function at headline scale. Intended for editorial, branding and motion work where a clean, purposeful sans with strong geometric roots is needed.

name: Sharp Grotesk
classification_notes: Neo-grotesque sans-serif rooted in 19th-century American wood type traditions and reinterpreted through Adrian Frutiger's systematic design methodology. Spans 21 width variants each in seven weights with italic support across most widths — an unusually broad tonal range for a single grotesque family.
summary: Sharp Type's flagship neo-grotesque: 21 widths, seven weights, and over 250 fonts drawing on 19th-century American wood type and Frutiger's systematic rigour.
description: Sharp Grotesk is a neo-grotesque family built from the traditions of 19th-century American wood type, reinterpreted through the systematic discipline of Adrian Frutiger's design process. It spans 21 width variants each in seven weights, with italics across most widths, giving designers a wide tonal range from tight condensed display to open editorial body setting. Extended in 2023 to cover Greek, Cyrillic, Thai and Hangul alongside the original Latin, it stands as one of the most complete grotesque families in contemporary use.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Grotesk is Sharp Type's defining sans-serif, inspired by the directness of 19th-century American wood type and the methodical discipline of Adrian Frutiger. The family covers 21 width variants across seven weights, with italic counterparts for most styles, totalling over 250 fonts. Language support was expanded in 2023 to include Greek, Cyrillic, Thai and Hangul.

name: Sharp Sans Condensed
classification_notes: A condensed-width humanist grotesque that carries the warm, approachable letter structure of the Sharp Sans family into tighter proportions. Clean terminals, optically adjusted spacing and a humanist baseline distinguish it from a strict neo-grotesque. The condensed format preserves the legibility and personality of the wider family in a narrower footprint.
summary: A condensed humanist grotesque from Sharp Type that brings the friendly clarity of Sharp Sans into a narrower width suited to headlines and space-constrained layouts.
description: Sharp Sans Condensed distils the humanist warmth of Sharp Type's Sharp Sans into a compressed format, running across seven weights from Thin to Extrabold with matching italics. The tighter proportions make it well-suited to display headlines, editorial mastheads and branding contexts where the full-width family would feel too expansive. It retains the clean terminal treatment and even stroke modulation that characterise the wider family.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type position Sharp Sans Condensed as the compressed counterpart to Sharp Sans, offering the same breadth of weights in a narrower form factor. Designed for display settings and situations requiring more text in less horizontal space, the family maintains the humanist character of the original across all seven weights.

name: Sharp Slab
classification_notes: Geometric Egyptian slab serif — rectangular serifs of uniform weight, consistent with the right-angle geometry of Sharp Sans. Shares identical proportions and weight range with Sharp Sans, making the two families interchangeable in layout without disrupting rhythm. Part of the Sharp Sans Superfamily alongside Sharp Sans Display No.1, Sharp Sans Display No.2, Sharp Sans, and Sharp Sans Condensed. No flared or bracketed serifs; the construction is clean and low-contrast throughout.
summary: The Egyptian slab serif companion to Sharp Sans, designed alongside Connor Davenport for the 2016 Hillary Clinton presidential campaign and built to handle every level of editorial typographic hierarchy.
description: Sharp Slab is an Egyptian slab serif developed as the final addition to the Sharp Sans Superfamily, a system conceived for editorial design and stress-tested on the 2016 Clinton presidential campaign. Designed by Lucas Sharp and Connor Davenport, it shares proportions and geometric logic with Sharp Sans, making the two families interchangeable in layouts without disturbing spacing or rhythm. Seven weights from Thin through ExtraBold, each with a matching italic, give it the range to cover display headlines, subheads and body text across both print and digital contexts.
foundry_blurb: The last addition to the Sharp Sans Collection – an Egyptian-slab serif companion to Sharp Sans, added when the 2016 Clinton campaign required a complete editorial system. Built for comprehensive typographic hierarchy and tested daily across headlines, banners, websites and print materials throughout a modern presidential campaign.

name: Sharp Sans Display No.2
classification_notes: One of two display sub-families preserved from the original Sharp Sans design when the family was redrawn in 2016. Geometric in structure with a humanist undertow. Specifically distinguished by drawn true italics rather than obliques, which set it apart from the redesigned Sharp Sans released the same year. Display-optimised spacing and proportions intended for headline and large-scale use.
summary: The second of two preserved display variants from Sharp Type's original Sharp Sans design, distinguished by true drawn italics and proportions tuned for headline scale.
description: Sharp Sans Display No.2 is a display-optimised geometric sans-serif from Sharp Type, preserved when Lucas Sharp redrawn the Sharp Sans family in 2016. Where the updated Sharp Sans moved forward, Display No.2 kept the proportions and character of the earlier design, including proper drawn italics rather than slanted romans. It sits alongside Display No.1 as a companion cut, both intended for large-scale headline and branding use where the true italic forms give typographers more expressive range.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Sans Display No.2 is one of two renamed variants from the original Sharp Sans design, preserved alongside the 2016 redrawn update. The Display cuts retain their distinctive true italics, separating them from the newer family and making them the choice when the original Sharp Sans character is needed at display sizes.

name: Simula
classification_notes: Humanist old-style text serif in the Plantin tradition. Distinctive single-story 'a' drawn from Plantin Infant. Moderate stroke contrast, warm texture, designed for sustained reading at text sizes. Not a revival – a contemporary interpretation of the old-style model.
summary: A Plantin-inspired text serif by Justin Sloane with a distinctive single-story 'a', developed over four years as a warm, literary reading face.
description: Simula is a humanist old-style text serif designed by Justin Sloane and released through Sharp Type in 2019, the result of four years of development and his debut typeface. The design draws loosely on Plantin, borrowing the single-story 'a' characteristic of Plantin Infant to give the face warmth and a slightly informal quality at small sizes. It has been adopted widely in editorial and digital contexts, typically paired with contemporary grotesques.
foundry_blurb: Sharp Type describes Simula as loosely inspired by Plantin, with a single-story 'a' in the manner of Plantin Infant. It was developed over four years by Justin Sloane as his first typeface release, balancing historical reference with contemporary sensibility for reading use.
